descriptionChirho: The core Qal active sense of לקח — to take, lay hold of, seize, or pick up a person or object; covers all inflections (perfect, imperfect, imperative, infinitive, participle) and persons of the basic transitive 'take' meaning, confirmed by Arabic أَخَذَ, Korean 취하다, and Swahili -chukua across all clusters.

To receive or accept something given or offered — distinguished from active 'take' by the volitional transfer from another party; confirmed by Arabic قَبُول (acceptance), Korean 받다 (receive), and Swahili -pokea (receive).

To go and get, to fetch, to bring someone or something — the motion-toward-speaker nuance of לקח where the emphasis is on conveying or delivering rather than grasping; confirmed by Arabic أَحْضِرْ (bring/fetch), Korean 데려오다/가져오다 (bring), and Swahili -leta (bring).
To take away or remove from someone, with a sense of dispossession or stripping — the ablative use of לקח; confirmed by Korean 빼앗다 (snatch away) and Spanish quitar (remove/take away).

Passive of the core 'take' sense — to be taken, be captured, be seized, or be carried away by another agent; confirmed by Arabic أُخِذَ (passive voice), Korean 취함 받다/취해졌다 (be taken), and Swahili -chukuliwa (passive).

The Hitpael of לקח meaning to flash back and forth, to flame or flicker — a specialized sense used of the flaming sword in Genesis 3:24, semantically distinct from all 'take' meanings; confirmed by Arabic مُتَّقِدَة (blazing), Korean 번쩍이는 (flashing), and Swahili -waka (blaze).
